thread:
alex: Heads-up — after rolling nvidia-container-toolkit v1.15 on the eu-west1 canaries, a few pods fail to start: libcuda/libnvidia-ml never get mounted and downstream jobs OOM or crash quickly. Repro log from node-3:

```
containerd: time="2026-03-16T09:12:34Z" level=error msg="failed to mount host path /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so: permission denied"
kubelet: E0316 09:12:35.123456 1 pod_container_deletor.go:56] "Killing container" err="failed to start container" containerID="..."
```

maya: Saw this on 3 nodes in the canary pool. containerd shows bind mount failing with EPERM. Init container logs show the init tried to set permissions then failed when doing a bind-propagation change.

sam: Interesting — overlayfs upperdir on our AMI is owned by root:root with mode 755. The toolkit init container switches namespaces and then tries to mount from host; if the mount propagation is rprivate we lose the bind. Could be a propagation/privileges ordering issue. Also saw "failed to resolve /run/nvidia/driver-518 -> no such file or directory"

devbot: deploy-bot: rollback requested for canary pool to toolkit v1.14 by @alex — started at 09:20 UTC

jen: Autoscaler drained 8 GPUs in eu-west1 because pods were failing liveness checks after crashes. That caused ~2 hours of queueing for batch jobs; preliminary cost delta ~+12% due to re-scheduling on on-demand nodes.

alex: Plan proposal:
- revert canary to v1.14 immediately
- add a privileged init variant that uses bind-propagation=rslave on the hostPath mounts as a temporary workaround
- add an e2e test matrix for overlayfs/kernel variants (kernel 6.1/6.2) before toolkit upgrades
- open incident and notify affected customers (org-42 batch, org-77 training)

maya: Quick patch: building image with init container set to run as privileged and mount with: --mount type=bind,src=/usr/lib,dst=/host/usr/lib,bind-propagation=rslave. Can test on node-3 in ~30m. If it fixes the bind, we can use it as a stopgap.

sam: Also seeing NCCL errors in ML tasks: "ncclUnhandledCudaError" followed by logs complaining nvmlInit() failed because libnvidia-ml.so missing. So this isn't just mounts failing; some runtime probes break and libs not present cause GPU drivers to mis-report and jobs abort.

jen: I'm scheduling a quick infra sync at 14:00 UTC to coordinate rollback and customer comms. Ops cost note: if we roll to CPU fallbacks for long, backfill runs will spike cloud spend.

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-007 — title: eu-west1 toolkit mount regression causing libcuda/libnvidia-ml absence — priority P2

alex: If the privileged init patch works on the canary, we still need a proper root cause: suspected interaction between toolkit v1.15's init ordering and overlayfs bind propagation on kernels with the recent overlayfs patches (kernel 6.2). Add kernel variant gating to our upgrade playbook. Also pause auto-toolkit upgrades across fleets.

maya: Canary test in progress — will report pass/fail in this thread. If it passes, we can roll the patch to the other canaries tonight and schedule a full rollback for the rest of the fleet tomorrow morning.

sam: FYI note for release engineering: avoid rolling toolkit when node kernel != validated-kernel-list. I'll add a check to the upgrade job and a small e2e with NVML probe.

alex: Good. Also track impacted jobs and owners so CS can proactively reach out.

jen: Thanks everyone — will run the customer blast if rollback happens.

maya: quick update — privileged init fixed the bind on node-3, libcuda now present and NVML probing passes. Pushing patch to remaining canaries now.

alex: 👍 Once canaries green, we still revert v1.15 from non-critical pools and draft postmortem. Add a note in release notes: "toolkit v1.15 incompatible with overlayfs variants on some kernels; do not auto-upgrade."
